script.title: Why Vodafone Idea Lost ₹5,975 Crore Despite Higher Revenue

segments.text: Vodafone Idea lost five thousand nine hundred crore rupees this quarter.
Here is the bizarre twist, yaar. Their quarterly revenue actually jumped 6.2 percent to over twelve thousand crore rupees.
How does a company collect more paisa from millions of smartphone users, yet sink deeper into the red? Let us decode the hidden math behind India's telecom battle.
segments.broll: slow motion person using smartphone street

segments.text: If millions of subscribers pay higher mobile bills every month, where is that cash going?
The problem starts with legacy debt and spectrum dues owed to the government. Interest payments alone eat up thousands of crores every single quarter.
Even though average bill sizes increased, network maintenance costs and tower rentals rose just as fast. It is like earning a higher salary but spending it all on old credit card bills.
While Vi bleeds cash on old loans, rivals are playing a brutal game of market dominance.
Jio and Airtel spent massive sums building nationwide 5G networks. To keep high-value customers, Vodafone Idea must match that spending without having spare cash.
If you enjoy deep dives into how Indian business giants make and lose money, hit that subscribe button right now.
When subscribers do not get fast 5G speeds in their area, they port their numbers out. Losing premium 4G users reduces total revenue potential even further over time.
Will India's telecom market permanently shrink into a rigid two-player duopoly?
The central government converted past interest dues into equity, becoming the largest shareholder in Vodafone Idea. Bank loan restructuring and equity rounds offer temporary breathing space.
Turning around an empire worth thousands of crores requires consistent subscriber growth and rapid network upgrades, not just financial relief.

script.description:
Vodafone Idea recently reported a massive Q2 net loss of ₹5,975 crore despite seeing its revenue rise by 6.2%. In this video, we break down the economics behind India's telecom industry and why high revenue does not always equal profit.

You will learn how spectrum debt, interest burdens, subscriber migration, and 5G capital expenditure trap struggling telecom operators in heavy cash burn.
